cells.tense: Vision is flowing here and now because what has been lived through has settled.
cells.act: move toward the thing you want, one step, today
cells.ask: Take one step today toward the thing you keep circling — not the plan, the step. Pick the direction that pulls rather than pushes, and go. You don't need the whole way visible to take the first of it.
cells.core:
You can head somewhere without seeing the whole route first. One real step on the light you have, and you read the ground as you go, because what you've been through has settled enough that the next move is a continuation rather than an invention. That's what makes it steady instead of certain.

Steadiness there isn't a closed door against wanting. There's a direction your attention keeps leaning toward, and you can move on it before the picture is finished. Let the first step teach you what the second one is. The fuller view can complete itself while you're already walking.
cells.sheetLine: You can move on the light you actually have.
cells.verb: Moving through uncertainty on the light you have

cells.tense: The imagined finish is standing where the tending should be, and the actual thing waits.
cells.act: tend it small and ask nothing of it
cells.ask: Set the finished picture aside for seven days. Take the smallest real piece you can put your hands on and tend only that — no result owed, no version to defend. Name what you're tending before you touch it.
cells.core:
The picture being held has run well past the life it's supposed to be about. What is being dreamed has its backstage built and its ending rehearsed, and the attention keeps going into the rehearsal instead of anything that can be touched. It looks like vision. From the side, it looks like something kept possible and left unattended.

There's a kind of care that doesn't lose the dreamer. Choose the smallest piece of this that exists nearby and look after just that for a week — nothing owed, nothing to protect. Whatever tries to promote itself back into the big picture gets told to wait. If the small thing grows, the picture will have something real to stand on. If it doesn't, the week wasn't spent inside a dream.

cells.tense: The literal answer is still held, and the room where the open question lived is behind.
cells.act: wait until you know which part matters, then begin with that part
cells.ask: Before you explain the next thing, sit with it for ten minutes. Don't argue it or translate it. Let the part that matters come forward quietly, and start there. A notebook helps only if it holds what came, not the case against it.
cells.core:
Something lands before the argument starts — a direct read on what matters, quick and quiet and unproven. You tend to distrust it. You want the plain fact, the literal version, the reading that can't be wrong, and that rules out the part that turns out true anyway. Not knowing is allowed to be a place you stand in rather than a door you shut fast.

Strangeness isn't the enemy either; it's often the signal that something real is underneath. Give the unproven read a few quiet minutes before you overrule it. Whichever perception stays when you've stopped pushing, that one has earned your next step. Begin with it.

cells.tense: The direction is being kept already, and the one keeping it has not signed the work.
cells.act: keep the steady light lit by attention, not flash
cells.ask: Do the plain version of what you already repeat — as much as usual, by yourself, no flourish. Something has been growing from it. Put a mark on a page each time, if you like; the marks are yours whether or not you keep them.
cells.core:
You're already repeating something — the same small motion, the same steadied attention, again and again — and it has been shaping how you move through loose ground. You just don't put your name on it. It gets filed as habit, or mood, or the way things happen around you. The direction is being kept either way. The only missing piece is counting it as yours.

So do the plain version again (today works), the one you'd do if nobody were watching, and keep it small enough to finish. This kind of steadiness doesn't need light or performance; it needs the one keeping it to say truthfully that they're keeping it. That practice is already how you find your way through the unclear parts. Sign it.
cells.sheetLine: You haven't signed a practice that is already yours.

attempts.check: The record does not say what the person has actually processed or failed to process, so asking for 'fully lived' experience is not supported; the clearer objection is that someone already fluent in slow, careful calibration may hear the balance cell as telling them to move faster than they know how. The asks survive a wrong read because looking longer, tending something small, attending to one thing, and repeating a small practice are all useful without the diagnosis (a seeker holding an empty feeling keeps the log; a literal person keeps the light lit). The sentence that serves the Writer more than the person is any line that turns the person into a symbol of their own dream; every core is written to say what the capacity is DOING and what they'll have, never what it is called, and the too-little cell says where they stand, not why.
